title: Measure the size and speed claims instead of repeating them
design:
'20x bigger, 2x slower' is unmeasured and suspiciously round. It appears to have been inherited from conversation rather than measured, which is a bad place to be found by the first reviewer who checks.

Benchmark pkix-path against rustls-webpki on the common TLS path -- the case both actually optimise -- and record binary size for a minimal verifier build. Minimal means default features, which for pkix-path is rsa + p256; comparing an all-features build against webpki would be measuring the wrong thing and would flatter nobody.

Report whatever the numbers are. If we are 20x bigger on a minimal verifier build that is worth knowing precisely, because the honest pitch is that the size buys policy trees, delta CRLs, OCSP, CT, DANE and attribute certificates -- none of which webpki set out to provide.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Throughput benchmark, pkix-path vs rustls-webpki, common TLS chain, same machine and inputs
[ ] Binary size for a minimal verifier build of each, method recorded
[ ] Numbers committed with the command that produced them, so they can be re-run rather than re-guessed
[ ] Any claim in the workspace's prose that cites unmeasured figures is corrected or deleted
